content.text: Now I'll run the temporal analysis: for each ingredient, count patients who had a *new* (first-ever) weight-gain code within 90 days after their first exposure to that drug. I'll use the OMOP `concept_ancestor` to catch all drug forms descending from each ingredient, and restrict weight-gain to non-pregnancy standard concepts.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH wg_concepts AS (
  SELECT descendant_concept_id AS cid
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor
  WHERE ancestor_concept_id = 439141  -- Abnormal weight gain (SNOMED standard)
),
wg_events AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS first_wg_date
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN wg_concepts w ON co.condition_concept_id = w.cid
  GROUP BY co.person_id
),
ing AS (
  SELECT c.concept_id, c.concept_name FROM omop.concept c
  WHERE c.concept_id IN (785788,800878,766814,735979,757688,703244,712615,40230761,
    725131,722031,710062,721724,778268,738156,797617,715939,739138,
    797399,734354,745466,751246,19124477,740275,
    1551099,1550557,1506270,1518254,975125,
    1353766,1307046,1314002,1332418,
    1500211,1300978,1436678,1110727,
    1559684,1560171,1597756,1525215,1547504)
),
drug_first AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, ca.ancestor_concept_id AS ing_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS first_rx
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON de.drug_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  JOIN ing ON ing.concept_id = ca.ancestor_concept_id
  GROUP BY de.person_id, ca.ancestor_concept_id
)
SELECT ing.concept_name AS drug,
  COUNT(DISTINCT df.person_id) AS n_exposed,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN we.first_wg_date >= df.first_rx
                       AND we.first_wg_date <= DATEADD(day,90,df.first_rx)
                       AND we.first_wg_date > df.first_rx THEN df.person_id END) AS n_new_wg_90d
FROM drug_first df
JOIN ing ON ing.concept_id = df.ing_id
LEFT JOIN wg_events we ON we.person_id = df.person_id
GROUP BY ing.concept_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT df.person_id) > 0
ORDER BY n_new_wg_90d DESC, n_exposed DESC

content.text: Found the bug: weight-gain codes live in the `observation` table, not `condition_occurrence`. My first query joined to conditions, hence all zeros. Let me rerun against `observation`.

  WHERE concept_id IN (785788,800878,766814,735979,757688,703244,712615,40230761,
    725131,722031,710062,721724,778268,738156,797617,715939,739138,

    1353766,1307046,1314002,1332418,
    1500211,1300978,1436678,1110727,
    1559684,1560171,1597756,1525215,1547504)
),
drug_first AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, ca.ancestor_concept_id AS ing_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS first_rx
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON de.drug_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  JOIN ing ON ing.concept_id = ca.ancestor_concept_id
  GROUP BY de.person_id, ca.ancestor_concept_id
)
SELECT ing.concept_name AS drug,
  COUNT(DISTINCT df.person_id) AS n_exposed,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN we.first_wg_date > df.first_rx
                       AND we.first_wg_date <= DATEADD(day,90,df.first_rx) THEN df.person_id END) AS n_new_wg_90d,
  CAST(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN we.first_wg_date > df.first_rx
                       AND we.first_wg_date <= DATEADD(day,90,df.first_rx) THEN df.person_id END)
       / COUNT(DISTINCT df.person_id) AS DECIMAL(5,2)) AS pct_new_wg_90d
FROM drug_first df
JOIN ing ON ing.concept_id = df.ing_id
LEFT JOIN wg_events we ON we.person_id = df.person_id

By rate, **second-generation antipsychotics** (lurasidone, paliperidone, clozapine, aripiprazole, risperidone) rise to the top — consistent with their established weight-gain liability.

## Caveats
- This is a temporal association, not causal: it counts a coded weight-gain observation after drug start; it doesn't adjust for indication, baseline BMI, concomitant drugs, or coding practice.
- Weight-gain **coding is rare overall** (rates <1%), so this reflects when a clinician *documented a code*, not measured weight change. A measured-weight (kg trajectory) analysis would be far more sensitive.
- The drug list was a curated set of known weight-gain-associated ingredients (antipsychotics, antidepressants, anticonvulsants, steroids, antidiabetics, etc.); the knowledge-graph schema/query timed out, so I used this clinical list rather than KG-derived associations.
